sentences.text: Cruschedula is an enigmatic bird genus containing only one species, Cruschedula revola, and is considered a nomen dubium, a name given to fossils too incomplete for reliable identification.
The genus Cruschedula was first described by Florentino Ameghino in 1899.
Ameghino named the genus Cruschedula by combining the words for "shin" and "a small sheet of paper".
The genus and species were originally described based on a single partial bone that Ameghino identified as a section of a tarsometatarsus, a leg bone found in birds.
The fossil was found in Oligocene beds of the Deseado Formation near the San Jorge Gulf in Southern Patagonia.
Ameghino initially created the family Cruschedulidae but later synonymized it into Cladornithidae in 1906.
Ameghino classified the fossil as a penguin because he believed it resembled other penguin fossils found in the same formation.
The time range for Cruschedula is estimated from 33.9 to 23.04 million years ago.
